newsitem.title: UK: A job free of the rat race - if you can keep quiet.
newsitem.headline: A job free of the rat race - if you can keep quiet.

text.p: Sister Mary Bernadette believes she can offer the ideal career to women wanting out of today's rat race, but only those able to stay silent for long periods should apply.

She is mounting a major poster campaign at Roman Catholic churches, schools and colleges to recruit nuns for contemplative convents following a decline in the number of women wanting to join closed orders, the Guardian reported on Thursday.
"We are doing this because we want to remind people that we are still here and because we are not getting that many young females who want to join us," Sister Bernadette, 68, told the newspaper.
"I think it is because we are becoming a secular society and because there's a lot more scope for women today. I mean they can even become prime minister..."
She is one of only nine sisters at the Redemptoristine Convent in the northwest English port city of Liverpool. The convent has not had a new vocation for more than 20 years.
The day starts at 5.30 a.m. when the nuns embark on a routine involving regular prayer sessions.
"We get an hour's break in the evening when we like to sit down to watch the news or videos," said Sister Bernadette, disclosing that detective movies were a favourite.
